content.comment_body: Hello, I’m interested in whether it’s possible to exchange data between two [product_name] controllers using AWS infrastructure. My requirement is that PLC 2 should execute some logic if a digital input is activated on PLC 1 (for example, pump station 1 should block pump station 2 when 'High Level' is detected). Is this feasible?

Hi, From my understanding, this can be done using AWS IoT Core. You might want to look for resources on sending data between two IoT devices via IoT Core. Another option could be using [product_name] communication modules, which may be a more cost-effective solution. See this link for more details: [url]
Hello, I’m looking for a similar solution. If you find any details about doing this with AWS, I’m interested as well. Thank you for your assistance.

analysis.insight_summary: Users are aiming to connect two [product_name] controllers so that logic can be executed in one device based on inputs from another, utilizing AWS infrastructure. The discussion shows there’s limited documentation or community experience for direct cloud-based interconnection of these devices with AWS. Suggested approaches include AWS IoT Core or using [product_name] modules, which might offer a simpler and more budget-friendly alternative. Users appear to be searching for well-integrated and officially supported solutions, as current documentation seems insufficient.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect [product_name] controllers to provide a reliable and straightforward way to exchange data using AWS, allowing for remote logic execution across devices without complicated setup or dependence on third-party solutions.
